seoContent.title: About These Dog Health Calculators
seoContent.intro: Our dog tools are built on peer-reviewed veterinary standards from AAHA, AAFCO, and WSAVA. Here's what each tool does — and why it matters for your dog's health.
seoContent.faq1: What is the most accurate dog age calculator?
seoContent.faq1Answer: Our dog age calculator uses the AAHA 2023 life stage guidelines, which account for breed size differences. Small dogs age slower than large dogs — a 5-year-old Chihuahua is roughly 36 human years, while a 5-year-old Great Dane is about 48.
seoContent.faq2: How do I calculate my dog's daily calorie needs?
seoContent.faq2Answer: Our calorie calculator uses the AAFCO Maintenance Energy Requirement (MER) formula: RER × activity multiplier. RER = 70 × (weight in kg)^0.75. The multiplier adjusts for neuter status, activity level, and life stage.
seoContent.faq3: Which vaccinations does my dog need?
seoContent.faq3Answer: Core vaccines (required for all dogs) include rabies, DHPP (distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, parainfluenza). Non-core vaccines like Bordetella and Leptospirosis depend on your region and lifestyle. Our schedule follows WSAVA 2024 guidelines.
seoContent.faq4Answer: Dogs are pregnant for approximately 63 days (9 weeks) from ovulation. Our gestation calculator shows the expected due date range and key developmental milestones from implantation through whelping.

seoContent.title: About These Cat Health Calculators
seoContent.intro: Built on AAHA/AAFP Feline Life Stage Guidelines and WSAVA vaccination standards. Every formula is cited and transparent.
seoContent.faq1: How old is my cat in human years?
seoContent.faq1Answer: Cats age differently from dogs and humans. A 1-year-old cat is roughly 15 human years. A 5-year-old cat is about 36. Our calculator uses the AAHA/AAFP feline life stage guidelines.
seoContent.faq2: Is my cat overweight? How to use the BCS scale?
seoContent.faq2Answer: The Body Condition Score (BCS) is a 1–9 scale developed by veterinarians. You can assess your cat at home by feeling their ribs and looking at their waist from above. 60% of indoor cats score above 5 (ideal). Our BCS tool guides you through the assessment and calculates a safe weight target.
seoContent.faq3: How much water should my cat drink daily?
seoContent.faq3Answer: Cats need approximately 50–60 ml of water per kg of body weight daily. Cats on dry food diets need more supplemental water. Our hydration calculator accounts for both dry and wet food intake.
seoContent.faq4: What vaccines does my indoor cat need?
seoContent.faq4Answer: Core vaccines for all cats include FVRCP (feline viral rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia) and rabies. Even indoor cats need these — the FVRCP series starts at 6–8 weeks with boosters every 3 years.
seoContent.faq5Answer: Cats are pregnant for approximately 65 days (range 61–72 days). Our gestation calculator provides the expected due date range and key veterinary milestones during pregnancy.

scienceSection.title: Why we don't use the "7× rule"
scienceSection.body: The popular "multiply by 7" formula has no scientific basis. Dogs mature rapidly in the first 2 years (reaching sexual maturity and full size), then age more slowly thereafter. Our calculator uses size-adjusted life stage guidelines from: the American Animal Hospital Association (AAHA) and the 2020 UCSD epigenetics methylation study (Labrador reference). Larger breeds age faster due to higher metabolic rates and faster cell division — not because of size itself.

scienceSection.title: The Science Behind Cat Aging
scienceSection.body: Cats age rapidly in their first 2 years of life — a 1-year-old cat is roughly equivalent to a 15-year-old human, and a 2-year-old cat is about 24 human years. After age 2, each cat year equals approximately 4 human years. This is based on the AAHA/AAFP Feline Life Stage Guidelines, which define six distinct life stages with different health and nutritional needs.

catHydration.title: Cat Hydration Calculator
catHydration.subtitle: Calculate how much water your cat needs daily. Accounts for moisture from dry and wet food.

result.totalMl: {name} needs about {ml} ml of water per day.
result.moistureNote: Dry food ~10% moisture · Wet food ~80% moisture
result.statusSlightlyLow: Slightly low — add a little more water
result.scienceBody: Cats evolved as desert animals and have a low thirst drive. In the wild, they get most of their water from prey (~70–80% moisture). Cats on dry-food-only diets are at highest risk of chronic dehydration, which can contribute to urinary tract disease and kidney problems. Providing fresh water daily and incorporating wet food are the two most effective strategies.
